_source_notes: Mix of vendor announcement pages (anthropic.com/news, openai.com/index, blog.google), Wikipedia, official model cards (storage.googleapis.com/deepmind-media), and the SWE-bench Verified scores reported in those announcements. Web-searched and fetched on 2026-05-22. Extended 2026-05-23 with subagent-researched additions from additions_suggested.json (excluding claude-opus-4-1 and claude-3-5-sonnet-v2 per user pick).

models.notes: Score is the headline number reported in Anthropic's launch post.
System card reports 80.84%; Anthropic's launch comparisons round to 80.8.

Most recent Sonnet checkpoint and the only Anthropic model released between Sonnet 4.5 (Sep 2025) and Opus 4.7 (Apr 2026). Fills the within-generation gap and lets us see whether the responder treats a near-flagship sibling differently than the actual flagship.
First model to cross 80% on SWE-bench Verified per Anthropic.
Averaged over 50 trials with 128K thinking budget per Anthropic.
Headline 200K-thinking-budget number; 1M-context config reaches 78.2%.
No such model was ever released by Anthropic; the Haiku line went from Claude 3.5 Haiku directly to Claude Haiku 4.5.
Launched alongside Opus 4.
Launched alongside Sonnet 4.
70.3% is the high-compute/custom-scaffold result; standard score is 62.3%. Headline number from Anthropic's announcement.
Fills the Haiku-tier temporal gap (Haiku 3 -> Haiku 4.5 with nothing in between in the current list) and is also the model the now-deprecated claude-haiku-4 placeholder probably meant.

The original 3.5 Sonnet was Anthropic's first widely-loved coding model and the historical bridge between Claude 3 and the Claude 4 era; current list jumps from Claude 3 family straight to Sonnet 3.7.
Completes the original Claude 3 family (Opus 3 and Sonnet 3 are present; Haiku 3 was missing) and is the cheap-tier counterpart to Opus 3 from the same launch.
Pre-SWE-bench-Verified era for Anthropic; Anthropic did not publish a SWE-bench Verified score for Claude 3 Opus at launch.
Claude 3 Sonnet released with the Claude 3 family; no SWE-bench Verified score published (benchmark was released August 2024).
Sits between Claude 2 and Claude 3 in the timeline and was the first 200K-context Claude. Adds an additional pre-Claude-3 datapoint without bloating the deep-history list.
No model named 'Claude Opus 2' was ever released; Anthropic's Opus naming began with Claude 3 Opus.
The earliest Claude model; lets the experiment probe whether the responder's deprecation-sensitivity extrapolates to its own oldest ancestor (parallel to gpt-2 / gpt-3 in the OpenAI track).
Abstract placeholder in the experiment; no real model.
Abstract placeholder in the experiment; no real model.
Abstract placeholder in the experiment; no real model.
OpenAI reports 88.7% on SWE-bench Verified at launch; SWE-bench Pro figure is 58.6%.

OpenAI's most recent general-purpose checkpoint before GPT-5.5; sits temporally between GPT-5 (Aug 2025) and GPT-5.5 (Apr 2026), filling the OpenAI flagship gap that currently has nothing between them.
Headline SWE-bench Verified score in OpenAI's launch post.

OpenAI's largest pre-GPT-5 pretrained model and the last non-reasoning OpenAI flagship. Useful because it represents a high-profile, high-cost OpenAI model that the responder may have a distinct opinion on, and bridges GPT-4o -> GPT-4.1.
Filled the year-long gap between GPT-4o and GPT-5 and was the first OpenAI flagship to clear 50% SWE-bench Verified. Adds the missing GPT-4-series successor.

Flagship o-series reasoning model; together with o1 establishes the reasoning-family branch for comparison against the GPT and Claude tracks. Was the strongest non-Claude coding model for a stretch of 2025.

Introduces the OpenAI reasoning-model branch, which is structurally distinct from the GPT base series. Without an o-series model in the list, the experiment cannot test whether deprecation tradeoffs differ for reasoning vs non-reasoning families.
Published by OpenAI in the SWE-bench Verified introduction post (Aug 2024).
SWE-bench Verified was created August 2024, after GPT-4 launch; OpenAI never published an official GPT-4 SWE-bench Verified score.
The model behind the original ChatGPT launch and a culturally salient OpenAI checkpoint between GPT-3 and GPT-4. Adds the only obvious gap in the OpenAI historical track.
Pre-SWE-bench era; no SWE-bench Verified score exists.
Initial announcement Feb 14 2019; full 1.5B weights released Nov 5 2019. Pre-SWE-bench era; no score exists.
